newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday on uncertainties about market direction, traders said.
The key September 1997 contract ended at 3,324 yuan ($401) per tonne, losing one yuan. It opened at 3,324 yuan, hitting an intraday low of 3,316 and a high of 3,330 yuan per tonne.
March did not trade, May fell 89 to 3,081 yuan, July rose two to 3,255, November three to 3,334 and the January 1998 contract three to 3,343.
Combined volume rose to 23,800 tonnes from 21,300 tonnes.
Most contracts opened little changed from Friday's close and consolidated around opening levels for most of the session.

"Investors are cautious about buying because of uncertainties about the direction of the market," one trader said. "A wait-and-see attitude dominated the day's trading, and is likely to last for the next couple of days."
Traders said they expected soybeans to move around current levels in the short term, with investors lacking interest in trading.
